speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you describe the neck swelling in terms of its location, size, and whether it has changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, it is crucial to determine if this new swelling could be a metastasis. Does the swelling feel hard and fixed to underlying structures, or is it soft and mobile?

speaker: Doctor
text: The swelling feels soft and mobile, not fixed to underlying structures.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the cystic nature and location on the nape of your neck, this is highly suggestive of a pilomatrixoma or an epidermoid cyst, but we must rule out other possibilities. Do you recall any minor trauma to that area prior to the swelling appearing, or have you noticed any pitting or dimpling of the skin over the mass?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms a subcutaneous cystic lesion, which is consistent with an epidermoid cyst or lipoma rather than metastatic disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Epidermoid cyst
